people.gloss: The silver candle by the painted screen, under the autumn stars (Đỗ Mục, Thu tịch)
people.role: Hall-mistress of Họa Tinh Đường since 1150, talismans painted with the Dipper in Mặc Yên soot
people.appearance: A slight, grey-haired woman in a black robe flecked with soot, who sits so still at the painting table that moths settle on her sleeves.
people.backstory: Kỷ Ngân Chúc was born in the dark-fungus village of Huyền Chi Thôn, the Hall's own, and is the founder Kỷ Thu Tịch's (ky_thu_tich) grand-niece. She ground ink for a thousand mornings before the founder let her hold a brush, and has painted the Pivot's Dipper talismans by the Silver Candle since 1100. The founder made the Hall in 910, sworn to the Pivot, and its talismans would not run in the rain (V059). That is why the Pivot's archive and its envoys use nothing else. When the founder died in 1150 she left the Hall to Kỷ Ngân Chúc with a key and an oath. The key opens a cedar box in the head's room. The oath is that the box is never opened while the Hall is the Pivot's. The box holds the founder's copy of Thorn and Ink Verses, a song art the Pivot has forbidden since it destroyed Cửu Thiều Cung (C005). The Hall's rain-fast ink comes from its blood-ink writ. She opened the box once, the night she took the oath, and has kept the oath since. The Hall's soot comes from the kilns of Mặc Yên in the vermilion pines, under her ink master Lăng Mặc Khanh (lang_mac_khanh).
people.wants: To find an heir who can keep the box shut, and to keep painting until the candle burns down.
people.secret: The rain-fast ink every talisman of the Hall carries is a forbidden song art with the blood taken out. Every copy of the Compact the Pivot's archive has made since 910 is written in it.

people.appearance: A tall woman with ink to the elbow and a boxwood seal on a cord, who talks while she paints, which no one else dares.
people.backstory: A fungus-gatherer's daughter from the Hall's village like her master Kỷ Ngân Chúc (ky_ngan_chuc), named by her for the same poem. She holds the Dipper Talisman Seal and paints most of what the Pivot buys. She believes the rain-fast ink is the founder's honest discovery, and she would like to sell it to every sect on the continent.

people.role: Ink master of the Mặc Yên soot kilns in the vermilion pines
people.appearance: A black-handed old charcoal burner with burnt eyebrows and a cabinet of a thousand ink sticks, each labelled with its year.
people.backstory: A charcoal burner's son from the dense pines of Mật Tùng Lâm, he keeps the Hall's soot kilns, the Mặc Yên, among the vermilion pines. They were built on the ash of the pitch town that burned in 712 (V055). He can tell the year an ink was made by its smell and the shine of a stroke. He keeps a stick from every year since 1100, and he has never been asked to use the gift on anything but forgeries. Kỷ Ngân Chúc (ky_ngan_chuc) is his master.

people.role: The Hall's resident ink-maker at the Pivot's seat, who supplies the archive of the Compact
people.appearance: A neat, soft-spoken clerk in Pivot grey with the Hall's black cord at his wrist.
people.backstory: A scribe's son from Khai Dương Thành, he has lived at the Pivot's seat since 1160 and grinds the rain-fast ink for Tàng Ước Các. Its keeper Sử Ngưng Mặc (su_ngung_mac) trusts no other ink. In 1195 the copyist Thích Minh Thư (thich_minh_thu) asked him for a night's ink "for a guard roll of Tinh Tủy Mạch". He ground it and wrote the request in his book, with the date.

people.role: Founder of Họa Tinh Đường (910); she painted the Dipper's stars and kept a forbidden book
people.backstory: A fungus-dyer's daughter who painted the Dipper as the Pivot's watchmen described it from Trích Tinh Phong (A084). In 910 she founded the Hall, sworn to the Pivot, and its talismans would not run in the rain (V059). She bought the book that made them so from a beggar in Khai Dương: a copy of Thorn and Ink Verses, carried out of Cửu Thiều Cung after its fall (C005). She left the Hall, the key and the oath to her grand-niece Kỷ Ngân Chúc (ky_ngan_chuc).

ties.note: her grand-niece and successor
